Virtual 2028 Ford Expedition Shows All the Refreshed Goodies Way Ahead of Time, Both Inside and Out
16 photos
Photo: AutoYa / YouTube
The Blue Oval company has recently showcased the Ford Expedition Tremor: Project Overland as a bespoke off-road-focused family adventure SUV. As such, are we surprised that the rumor mill is thinking more extensively about the fifth generation of the full-size SUV?
The model, which has been around since the 1997 model year, competing with models like the Chevrolet Tahoe and Suburban or GMC Yukon and Yukon XL along with others like the Toyota Sequoia, Nissan Armada, and the Jeep (Grand) Wagoneer, came to life with its fifth iteration approximately two years ago, in October 2024.
Since then, it has attracted a new fanbase thanks to the new Ford Split Gate similar to the liftgates of a Range Rover or Lexus LX, and rides on the Ford T3 platform alongside the Ford F-150 and Lincoln Navigator with the Ford EcoBoost D35 3.5-liter twin-turbo V6 churning out 400 hp and 480 lb-ft of torque or 650 Nm for the base models or 440 hp in high-output versions.
The company has also focused on it just recently with Project Overland based on the Expedition Tremor, making it more than ready to leave the pavement behind for some off-road fun as a preview of potential factory-backed accessories and off-road packages focused on overlanding adventures. But if that’s not all?
Most likely because of all the commotion surrounding the new idea, the good folks over at the " AutoYa " info channel on YouTube have also unofficially imagined the CGI look of the facelifted 2028 Ford Expedition family-adventure SUV, with the host believing that next year, for the 2028 model year, the Blue Oval company might usher in an update of the full-size SUV to better compete with the refreshed Chevy Tahoe and GMC Yukon or to prepare for their next-generation models.
The line of thought is both for the regular Ford Expedition and the long-wheelbase Expedition Max as a mid-cycle refresh procedure for the ongoing fifth generation. The host believes the massive family-oriented SUV will receive both a front-end redesign with a new lighting signature and ample changes to the bumpers and grille, as well as some interior changes.
That’s where their resident member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators intervenes and stops dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to prepare their latest unofficial, hypothetical design project – the facelifted 2028 Ford Expedition. It comes with all those changes in a quick comparison reel, both outside and inside, plus there are also numerous color options for both the interior and exterior, as per tradition.
So, what do you think? Should Ford already move to upgrade and update the Expedition and Expedition Max for the 2028 model year as a potential measure to counter in advance the arrival of a hypothetical new generation of the Chevy Tahoe and GMC Yukon, or should they delay the facelift a little longer?
